question: Given the same planning request on the same planned-but-unbuilt app, does the kit on this branch make a model cut pass 1 into more issues, each one something the person can try, than the kit on main (06b0b92) or no kit at all?
machine: cloud-linux: Claude Code cloud container, Linux 6.18, Node 22.23.5, Claude Code 2.1.330, signed in with the owner's own login (no API key)
command: node research/agile-flow/runs/2026-11-23-plan-grain/measure.mjs --model <model id> --n <runs per arm> --main-kit <a checkout of main at 06b0b92 with cli/kit bundled>

metrics.name: units
metrics.how: lines that start with '- ' under the '## Build order' heading the prompt asks for: the issues the plan would open for pass 1

metrics.name: tryable_units
metrics.how: of those lines, the ones whose text after ' :: ' is not empty and does not start with the word nothing

metrics.name: steps_table
metrics.how: 1 when the pyramid skill's check-plan.mjs finds a steps table in the plan, else 0

metrics.name: checker_errors
metrics.how: errors check-plan.mjs reports, when there is a steps table

metrics.name: cost_usd
metrics.how: Claude Code's own estimate for the run, not a bill

metrics.name: turns
metrics.how: num_turns in Claude Code's result event

notes: Iterations: 5 per arm on claude-haiku-5-5, the model the kit's evals run on in CI. 3 per arm on claude-fable-5-2, the kit's planning tier, because each run costs more. If a model is skipped or cut short, the summary says so.
One prompt for every arm, in measure.mjs. It asks for the plan plus a '## Build order' list in a fixed form, so the count means the same thing in every arm.
The fixture is evals/lib/flatshare.mjs: four MVP slices, approved wireframes, and a profile and decision that say which model plans.
Limits per run: 20 turns, 420 seconds, a budget of 0.50 USD on Haiku and 2.00 USD on Fable (--budget).
A run that hits a limit but leaves a plan with a Build order still counts: the plan is what is measured. A run that leaves none is a failed row.
No warm-up: each run is a fresh session in a fresh temp folder.
The three arms of one iteration run at the same time. Iterations run one after another.
Effort is whatever Claude Code's headless default is for the model. The runs don't set it, and the result event doesn't report it.

versions.kit-branch: this branch at the commit that adds this manifest (0.4.0 plus the changes in this pull request)
